title: Wi-Fi drops when walking between floors
symptom: A laptop's Wi-Fi drops briefly when the user walks between floors
user_description: When I carry my laptop from the second floor to the meeting room upstairs, my call drops and Wi-Fi reconnects. Is my laptop faulty?

options.text: Tell her not to walk around during calls
options.why: Avoids the problem instead of fixing it.
Not practical, and the problem is how Wi-Fi hands over between areas.

options.text: Turn off Wi-Fi security so it connects faster
options.why: Makes the network unsafe and is not the cause.

options.text: Check whether it is one device or many and update her Wi-Fi driver. If many devices drop, report the exact spots to the network team, since moving between access points (roaming) may need tuning
options.why: One device points to its driver. Many devices point to how access points hand over, which the network team can adjust.

hints: Is it only her laptop, or others too?
What happens when a laptop moves from one access point to another?
What details would help the network team?
real_world_tip: Ask a colleague to walk the same route with their laptop. If theirs drops too, it is the network, not her laptop.
